hero.headline: Woman charged with inhaling nitrous oxide in parking lot of Port St. Lucie Police Department
hero.body:
A woman was arrested Thursday after police say she was inhaling nitrous oxide in the parking lot of the Port St. Lucie Police Department. The incident occurred at the police department facility in Port St. Lucie.

Authorities charged the woman with inhaling nitrous oxide, also known as huffing, which is illegal in Florida. The arrest took place in the parking lot of the police headquarters, according to reports.

Port St. Lucie police officers responded to the scene and took the woman into custody. The woman faces criminal charges related to the inhaling of nitrous oxide.

The arrest highlights ongoing concerns about substance abuse in St. Lucie County. Port St. Lucie Police Department has not released additional information about the case.

cards.headline: New Aldi opens in Hobe Sound as grocery prices rise 2.8% in 2026
cards.teaser: A new Aldi grocery store opened Thursday at 8867 Southeast Bridge Road in Hobe Sound, offering Martin County shoppers another option as food costs continue to c.
cards.body:
A new Aldi grocery store opened Thursday at 8867 Southeast Bridge Road in Hobe Sound, bringing more affordable choices to Martin County customers facing tight budgets. Cheryl and Tony Cooperman said they are excited to have an affordable option close to their home. Cheryl Cooperman said grocery prices are getting expensive and are changing the way she shops. She said they never used to look at prices but now go with what is on sale instead of what they want.

The opening comes as the USDA expects grocery prices to rise 2.8% this year. Fruits and vegetables are seeing an increase of less than 1%. Egg prices are dropping and beef prices fell 1.3% from April to May, though wholesale beef prices remain at all-time highs for this time of year. Pork rose 1% from April to May and chicken prices rose 1.3% over the same period. Shoppers James and Harry said Thursday they do not expect relief at the register anytime soon. They said prices are going to stay inflated and are not going to go down. They said stores like Aldi, which often have lower prices than other stores, can make a difference for everyday shoppers because there is nobody who is not feeling the price increase.

cards.headline: Treasure Coast Traffic Report: Major Ramp and Road Closures Planned July 12-17
cards.teaser:
Motorists should prepare for overnight interstate ramp closures, extended neighborhood road closures and lane restrictions across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties.

Driv
cards.body:
Motorists should prepare for overnight interstate ramp closures, extended neighborhood road closures and lane restrictions across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties.

Drivers across the Treasure Coast could encounter delays during the week of July 10-17 as construction and maintenance continue on several major roadways.

The Florida Department of Transportation's latest weekly traffic report identifies multiple lane restrictions across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties. FDOT placed additional emphasis on full road, ramp and bridge closures expected to have the greatest effect on motorists.

## Major closures to know about

### I-95 exit to Bridge Road closing overnight in Martin County

The southbound Interstate 95 exit ramp to County Road 708, also known as Bridge Road, at Exit 96 will be closed from **8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, July 12, through Thursday, July 16.**

Drivers will be directed to exit at Kanner Highway, travel south on Pratt Whitney Road and then head east on Bridge Road.

The closure is needed for roadway construction. Weather-related contingency dates are scheduled for July 19-23.

### Port St. Lucie neighborhood roads could close for several days

Extended closures are planned along several side streets near the SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard widening project.

Closures may begin at **7 a.m. Monday, July 13, and continue until 5 p.m. Friday, July 17,** on portions of SW Jaslo Avenue, SW Jacoby Avenue, SW McCullough Avenue, SW McCall Road and SW McHord Avenue.

The roads will close intermittently for drainage and utility installation. FDOT said adjacent roads will not be closed at the same time, and access to homes and businesses will be maintained.

Detours will generally use SW Paar Drive, SW McCain Street, SW McIntyre Street, SW Kabane Street and other nearby roads, depending on the closure location.

### I-95 ramp to Orange Avenue closing in Fort Pierce

The northbound I-95 exit ramp to westbound State Road 68, or Orange Avenue, will be closed from **8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, July 12, through Thursday, July 16.**

Motorists will be detoured using the exit to eastbound Orange Avenue, northbound Jenkins Road and westbound Loop Road before returning to westbound Orange Avenue.

The work includes paving and lighting installation. Contingency dates are July 19-23.

## Martin County traffic impacts

Motorists should expect overnight lane closures on I-95 between Bridge Road and the Martin-St. Lucie county line. Up to two lanes may close in each direction during overnight hours for milling, resurfacing and signage work.

On U.S. 1 in Stuart, two lanes may close intermittently between Fischer Street and Decker Avenue from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday through Friday for sign installation.

A1A between Shore Village Terrace and the Jensen Beach Causeway may be reduced to one lane at times from Monday through Friday for drainage work and pavement widening. Flaggers will maintain two-way traffic through the work zone.

Martin Highway between Stuart West Boulevard and Citrus Boulevard may also have intermittent overnight lane closures Tuesday through Thursday.

FDOT is additionally warning drivers in advance about several upcoming I-95 ramp closures at Martin Highway and Kanner Highway later in July and early August.

## St. Lucie County traffic impacts

Port St. Lucie Boulevard between Seafury Lane and Lennard Road may have daytime lane closures Monday through Friday. Two lanes may close overnight from Sunday through Friday for drainage work, milling and repaving.

U.S. 1 between Jennings Road and Golden Oak Trail may also have lane restrictions during both daytime and overnight hours.

On SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard, one lane may close between Jordin Avenue and Alcantarra Boulevard from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday through Friday as crews continue the widening project.

Up to two lanes may close overnight on I-95 between Glades Cut-Off Road and the area just south of Okeechobee Road for milling and repaving.

Midway Road between Florida's Turnpike and Selvitz Road may continue to have intermittent weekday lane closures through September as part of the roadway widening project.

## North Causeway marine restrictions

The new A1A North Causeway Bridge remains open to vehicle traffic, but significant restrictions are planned for boaters using the Intracoastal Waterway.

The existing drawbridge will not open to marine traffic from 7 a.m. Thursday, July 16, through 6 p.m. Saturday, July 18. Boats capable of passing beneath the bridge without an opening may continue through.

Additional single-leaf openings, partial channel obstructions and temporary full channel closures are scheduled through July 24 as crews remove portions of the former drawbridge.

FDOT said the marine work will not affect vehicle traffic on the new bridge.

## Indian River County traffic impacts

One lane may remain closed on the 17th Street bridges between Indian River Boulevard and Indian Bay Drive as bridge rehabilitation continues.

At the new I-95 interchange at Oslo Road, one or two interstate lanes may close overnight Sunday through Thursday for bridge work, milling and resurfacing.

On 90th Avenue between Sebastian Boulevard and 87th Street, one lane may close overnight Sunday through Friday for construction associated with the 85th Street widening project.

Drivers traveling near Sebastian Inlet should also expect intermittent lane or shoulder closures on A1A through Friday, July 17. Flaggers will direct motorists through the work zone.

Sections of the north and south parking lots at Sebastian Inlet State Park will remain closed during construction of the new bridge. The closures are expected to continue through spring 2032, although the park and portions of both parking lots remain open.

## Plan ahead

Construction schedules may change because of weather or other unforeseen conditions. Motorists should allow additional travel time, follow posted detours and use caution around workers and equipment.

Real-time interstate traffic conditions are available through Florida 511. Updated lane closure information is also available through FDOT District Four.

cards.headline: Florida's Month-Long Back-to-School Tax Holiday Begins July 20, Offers Savings on Clothing, Computers and School Supplies
cards.body:
Florida families can save hundreds of dollars during the state's annual back-to-school sales tax holiday, which runs from July 20 through Aug. 20, 2026. The 32-day tax-free shopping period eliminates sales tax on essential items families need for the new school year, with no sales tax due on qualifying purchases.

Clothing items under $100 per item qualify for the exemption, including shirts, pants, dresses, shoes, uniforms and athletic wear. Backpacks, handbags, diaper bags and fanny packs are tax-free, along with accessories such as wallets, belts, ties and graduation caps and gowns. Excluded items include briefcases, suitcases, watches, jewelry, skis, swim fins, roller blades and any clothing item over $100. School supplies under $50 per item are tax-free, including pens, pencils, erasers, crayons, notebooks, binders, folders, construction paper, poster board, markers, scissors, glue, tape, staplers, lunch boxes and composition books. Computer disks limited to blank CDs also qualify, along with flashcards, learning cards, jigsaw puzzles, puzzle books, interactive books, educational toys, memory and matching games, stacking blocks and educational sets under $30 per item.

Qualifying computers and accessories under $1,500 per item include laptops, desktops, tablets, electronic book readers and calculators. Tax-free accessories include keyboards, mice, monitors without TV tuners, printers, ink cartridges, modems, routers, cables, educational and productivity software, storage devices and memory cards. Computers must be for personal, non-commercial use, as business purchases do not qualify. Items ordered online during the holiday period qualify for the exemption even if delivered after Aug. 20. If shoppers buy an eligible item during the holiday and later exchange it for the same item in a different size or color, no tax applies to the exchange. Gift cards can be used to purchase eligible items during the holiday for the exemption, regardless of when the gift card was purchased.

The tax exemption is not available at theme parks and entertainment complexes, hotels and public lodging establishments, or airports. Florida retailers have no option to opt out of the sales tax holiday, and all qualifying purchases must be processed tax-free during the designated period. A family spending $500 on qualifying items could save $35 in sales tax. Items purchased with rain checks issued during the holiday period remain tax-free, and items qualify for layaway if shoppers take delivery during the holiday or put eligible items on layaway during the holiday even if final payment comes later. Items normally sold together must be purchased as a set and cannot be split up to meet price thresholds.

cards.headline: New Aldi opens on Southeast Bridge Road in Hobe Sound as grocery prices rise
cards.body:
A new Aldi opened Thursday at 8867 Southeast Bridge Road in Hobe Sound, offering Martin County shoppers an affordable grocery option as food costs continue to strain family budgets. Customers Cheryl and Tony Cooperman said they are excited to have the discount grocery chain close to their home. Cheryl Cooperman said she and her husband are thrilled to have it there and now have something with reasonable prices that is close by. She said grocery prices are getting expensive and are starting to change the way she shops. She said they are the type of people who never used to look at prices but now she will go with what is on sale instead of just with what they want, and they never used to do that.

The opening comes as the USDA expects grocery prices to rise 2.8% this year. Fruits and vegetables are seeing an increase of less than 1%. Egg prices are dropping and beef prices fell 1.3% from April to May, though wholesale beef prices remain at all-time highs for this time of year. Pork rose 1% from April to May and chicken prices rose 1.3% over the same period.

Shoppers James and Harry said Thursday they do not expect relief at the register anytime soon. They said prices are going to stay inflated and are not going to go down, and they would be willing to bet on that. They said stores like Aldi, which often have lower prices than other stores, can make a difference for everyday shoppers.

They said having stuff like this for the average person is extremely beneficial because there is nobody who is not feeling the price increase. The new location brings more affordable choices to customers already facing tight budgets as prices at the grocery store continue to put a strain on family budgets.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie ranked 67th most stressed city in U.S., 42nd worst for financial stress
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie was tabbed as the 67th most stressed city in the United States, with the city ranking 42nd most financially stressed in America, according to a WalletHub study released this month.
cards.body:
A new study released this month by WalletHub examined stress levels across American cities, and Port St. Lucie landed at number 67 for overall stress in the nation. The city also ranked 42nd for financial stress specifically. The study compared 182 cities across 39 metrics, including average weekly work hours, unemployment rate, divorce and suicide rates. Compared to other states, Florida performed fairly well, with no cities in the top 35. Jacksonville is the most stressed city in the Sunshine State, ranking 37th in the U.S.

In South Florida, Miami was listed at 50th with affordable housing ranked fourth worst in the U.S. Fort Lauderdale ranked 83rd. The report found that money, health and the economy all remain top stressors. The most stressed cities in the U.S. were Detroit, Baltimore, Cleveland, Memphis and Shreveport, Louisiana.

Wallethub analyst Chip Lupo said some stress is out of our control, due to issues with family, friends or employers. However, where you live can play a big role in how stressed you are. "Cities with high crime rates, weak economies, less effective public health and congested transportation systems naturally lead to elevated stress levels for residents. When moving, it's important to consider how a certain city may impact your mental health – not just your financial opportunities," Lupo said.

For those seeking less stressful environments, the study identified several options. Fremont, California, in the Bay Area, topped the list of least stressed cities. The notably affluent area has average home prices of about $1.5 million. South Burlington, Vermont, came in second, followed by Bismarck and Fargo, both in North Dakota. The full report is available on WalletHub's website for those interested in seeing how other cities ranked.

cards.headline: Park Vista Cobras Football Eyes State Playoffs After Strong 2025 Finish
cards.body:
Park Vista Community High School's football team is building on late-season momentum as the Cobras set their sights on the state playoffs in 2026. The team struggled to find their footing early in 2025 but finished strong, winning four of their last five games. Senior Harris Bender said the team felt good throughout the second half of that season. The Cobras are working towards being able to carry that performance through the whole season, and Bender said they have all the pieces in place now and it's just about executing. The ultimate goal is the state playoffs and eventually a state title, something the program has not achieved since 2017.

Park Vista head football coach Donald Hanna said the team has to take it one game at a time and cannot look past anyone. Hanna said the Cobras have to handle business weekly and if they do that and do their job, that will get them into the playoffs. Senior Erik Lee said coming in, he feels like the team has the guys needed to get it done, but they also have to put the work in to get there as well. Senior Justice Jones said it's going to feel amazing because he already knows it's going to happen. Park Vista opens the 2026 season on the road against Atlantic in August.

cards.headline: Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse offers 165 years of history with 105-step climb to Atlantic views
cards.teaser: Standing at the base of the Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse, visitors can admire its striking red brick tower rising high above the inlet. Built in 1860, the lighthouse has guided countless ships along Florida's Atlantic coast for more than 165 years.
cards.body:
The 105-step climb to the top was well worth every step. As visitors make their way up the narrow spiral staircase, they can imagine the lighthouse keepers who climbed these same stairs night after night, keeping the powerful Fresnel lens shining for mariners. Reaching the gallery, visitors are rewarded with breathtaking panoramic views. The Atlantic Ocean stretches endlessly to the east, while the turquoise waters of the Jupiter Inlet meet the Loxahatchee and Indian rivers below. Boats glide through the channel, and the sea breeze makes the warm Florida morning feel perfect.

After the climb, visitors can explore the museum grounds. Walking among the restored historic buildings, they can learn about the lighthouse's fascinating past from its construction before the Civil War to its years as an active Coast Guard station. The striking red brick tower was built in 1860 and has guided countless ships along Florida's Atlantic coast for more than 165 years.

hero.headline: Karolina Muchova Defeats Coco Gauff to Reach Wimbledon Final
hero.teaser: Karolina Muchova ended Coco Gauff's run at Wimbledon with a 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 victory Thursday that ended with a drama-filled tiebreaker.
hero.body:
Karolina Muchova ended Coco Gauff's run at Wimbledon with a 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 (10) victory Thursday that ended with a drama-filled tiebreaker, to become the fourth Czech woman in the last six years to reach the final of the grass-court Grand Slam. It will be the ninth-ranked Muchova's second Grand Slam final after losing to Iga Swiatek in the 2023 French Open championship match. The other Czech women in the Wimbledon final recently were Karolina Pliskova, who was runner-up in 2021, Marketa Vondrousova, who won the championship in 2023, and Barbora Krejcikova, who won the championship in 2024.

Muchova could face another Czech player in Saturday's final, with Linda Noskova to play Marta Kostyuk of Ukraine in the other semifinal next on Centre Court. For Gauff, it was still her most successful Wimbledon. Previously, the seventh-ranked American had gone only as far as the fourth round three times, including during her breakthrough run as a 15-year-old in 2019. The men's semifinals on Friday feature top-ranked and defending champion Jannik Sinner against seven-time Wimbledon winner Novak Djokovic and French Open champion Alexander Zverev against British wild card Arthur Fery.

cards.headline: Women's Professional Baseball League Unveils Team Names and Logos
cards.teaser: The Women's Professional Baseball League revealed the nicknames and logos of its four teams ahead of its inaugural season beginning Aug. 1 in Springfield, Illinois.
cards.body:
The Women's Professional Baseball League on Wednesday unveiled the nicknames and logos of its four teams ahead of its inaugural season, with each team name inspired by pioneering women. The four teams are the San Francisco Firebells, Los Angeles Queens, New York Heights and Boston Hunters.

Kelsie Whitmore, the first overall pick in the WPBL's inaugural draft, will play for the San Francisco Firebells. Mo'ne Davis will play center field for the Los Angeles Queens, along with veteran Japanese pitcher Ayami Sato. The WPBL's debut season begins on Aug. 1 in Springfield, Illinois, with games played at Robin Roberts Stadium, and will run through the second half of September, including a regular season and playoffs.

Whitmore told The Associated Press at a scrimmage in March that this is every little girl's dream to play professional baseball. The league hopes to create a space for women's baseball players similar to the one the All-American Girls Professional Baseball League did 70 years ago. Each team name holds unique meaning, with the New York Heights inspired by civil rights leader Dorothy Irene Height, the San Francisco Firebells by Lillie Hitchcock Coit, the Los Angeles Queens by baseball pioneer Lizzie Murphy, and the Boston Hunters by physician Harriot K. Hunt.

hero.headline: 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival Returns to Vero Beach This November
hero.body:
Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. is bringing the 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival back to Vero Beach this November. The event marks nearly two decades of the festival's presence in Indian River County.

The festival celebrates seafood and coastal culture on the Treasure Coast. Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. organizes the annual event, which has become a regular fixture in Vero Beach's fall calendar.

The 2026 festival will be held in November, though specific dates have not yet been announced. This year's event continues the tradition established in previous years of showcasing local and regional seafood offerings.

Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. oversees the festival's organization and planning. Additional details about vendor participation, entertainment and specific event dates are expected to be announced as the November date approaches.

hero.headline: Florida's Month-Long Back-to-School Tax Holiday Begins July 20, Offers Savings on Clothing, Computers and School Supplies
hero.body:
Florida families can save hundreds of dollars during the state's annual back-to-school sales tax holiday, which runs from July 20 through Aug. 20, 2026. The 32-day tax-free shopping period eliminates sales tax on essential items families need for the new school year, with no sales tax due on qualifying purchases.

Clothing items under $100 per item qualify for the exemption, including shirts, pants, dresses, shoes, uniforms and athletic wear. Backpacks, handbags, diaper bags and fanny packs are tax-free, along with accessories such as wallets, belts, ties and graduation caps and gowns. Excluded items include briefcases, suitcases, watches, jewelry, skis, swim fins, roller blades and any clothing item over $100. School supplies under $50 per item are tax-free, including pens, pencils, erasers, crayons, notebooks, binders, folders, construction paper, poster board, markers, scissors, glue, tape, staplers, lunch boxes and composition books. Computer disks limited to blank CDs also qualify, along with flashcards, learning cards, jigsaw puzzles, puzzle books, interactive books, educational toys, memory and matching games, stacking blocks and educational sets under $30 per item.

Qualifying computers and accessories under $1,500 per item include laptops, desktops, tablets, electronic book readers and calculators. Tax-free accessories include keyboards, mice, monitors without TV tuners, printers, ink cartridges, modems, routers, cables, educational and productivity software, storage devices and memory cards. Computers must be for personal, non-commercial use, as business purchases do not qualify. Items ordered online during the holiday period qualify for the exemption even if delivered after Aug. 20. If shoppers buy an eligible item during the holiday and later exchange it for the same item in a different size or color, no tax applies to the exchange. Gift cards can be used to purchase eligible items during the holiday for the exemption, regardless of when the gift card was purchased.

The tax exemption is not available at theme parks and entertainment complexes, hotels and public lodging establishments, or airports. Florida retailers have no option to opt out of the sales tax holiday, and all qualifying purchases must be processed tax-free during the designated period. A family spending $500 on qualifying items could save $35 in sales tax. Items purchased with rain checks issued during the holiday period remain tax-free, and items qualify for layaway if shoppers take delivery during the holiday or put eligible items on layaway during the holiday even if final payment comes later. Items normally sold together must be purchased as a set and cannot be split up to meet price thresholds.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie ranks 67th most stressed city in US, 42nd for financial stress
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie ranked as the 67th most stressed city in the United States according to a WalletHub study released this month. The study compared 182 cities across 39 metrics including average weekly work hours, unemployment rate, divorce and suicide rates.

The report cited Port St. Lucie as the 42nd most financially stressed city in America. Among Florida cities, Jacksonville topped the state at 37th nationally, followed by Miami at 50th and Fort Lauderdale at 83rd. No Florida cities appeared in the top 35 most stressed nationwide. Miami ranked fourth worst in the nation for affordable housing.

WalletHub analyst Chip Lupo said cities with high crime rates, weak economies, less effective public health and congested transportation systems naturally lead to elevated stress levels for residents. He noted that while some stress comes from issues with family, friends or employers that are beyond individual control, where you live can play a big role in stress levels. Lupo said it's important to consider how a city may impact mental health and not just financial opportunities when moving. The report found that money, health and the economy all remain top stressors.

Detroit, Baltimore, Cleveland, Memphis and Shreveport, Louisiana topped the list of most stressed cities in the United States. Fremont, California ranked as the least stressed city, followed by South Burlington, Vermont and Bismarck and Fargo, North Dakota. Fremont is located in the Bay Area and is notably affluent with average home prices of about $1.5 million.
